The still shore of a small woodland lake, water-lilies scattered across glassy faintly-luminous water, the whole canopy reflected without a ripple, a leaning willow trailing its branches into its own mirror image.

A glass-clear brook-bend with mossy emerald banks, smooth stepping stones crossing the shallows, foxgloves and forget-me-nots crowding right to the water's edge, ancient oaks arching protectively overhead.
A slow river winding through a meadow foaming with white and blush wildflowers, its surface catching soft light like poured silver, glowing birch trunks lining the far bank.
A ferny glen beneath a low waterfall, the pool breathing the softest spray over moss-cushioned boulders, a single sunbeam falling through the canopy gap to light the water from within.
A lily-pond cupped in ancient woodland, its surface a perfect mirror of green-gold canopy light, white blooms floating motionless, trailing willows encircling the banks in a curtain of silver-green.
A wildflower meadow lapping at the hem of an oak wood, drifts of cornflower and campion rising like blue and rose-coloured water, the tree-line glowing dark and sweet behind.
A blossom grove where fallen cherry petals carpet the grass in soft drifts of pale pink, overhead branches interlacing in a vault of white and blush, the air trembling with sweetness.

A glass-clear stream curving through a mossy bank scattered with primroses and wild violet, stepping stones half-submerged in the shallows, birch trees leaning close to watch their own pale reflections.
A mossy fern glen where an emerald boulder-field cradles a threading rill, the water barely audible beneath the ferns, soft light filtering through the canopy to glow on every wet stone.
A slow river bending lazily through a flower-foamed meadow, ox-eye daisies and red clover crowding both banks, the water lying like hammered pewter beneath a canopy of arching willows.
A forest clearing ringed by ancient oaks whose branches close overhead in a cathedral arch, the floor deep with bluebells, a shallow pool at the centre holding still sky and trembling starlight.

A small luminous lake at the forest's heart, its water faintly glowing as though lit from below, water-lilies drifting in slow circles, the surrounding beeches mirrored perfectly in its silver surface.

A waterfall pool fringed with hart's-tongue fern and pale wood anemones, the falling water a soft white ribbon, spray drifting across moss-cushioned stones, a gap in the canopy pouring warm gold light down.
A wildflower meadow rolling to a wood's dark edge, seas of oxeye daisy and clover moving gently as water, ancient hazels and oaks forming a deep green wall behind the blossoming.

A blossom grove of wild apple and cherry, petals lying knee-deep on the grass, branches overhead weighted with white and blush flowers, a narrow rill threading silver through the carpet of fallen bloom.

A glass-clear stream slipping over pale pebbles at a wide lazy bend, meadowsweet and watercress crowding the banks, old willows trailing fingertips into the current, reflections rippling in soft golden light.

A mossy fern glen floored with deep emerald cushions, a thin rill catching light between boulders draped in velvet moss, ancient ferns arching overhead, the whole hollow faintly luminous with filtered green.
A forest clearing ringed by silver birches whose bark glows white as moonlight, the floor soft with wild thyme and wood sorrel, a still pool at the heart reflecting every pale trunk.
A slow river winding through meadow grass foaming with meadowsweet and ragged robin, the current barely perceptible, the far bank lined with willows that trail long fingers into the luminous water.

A waterfall pool half-hidden by overhanging ferns, the water trembling with soft perpetual spray, sunbeams piercing the canopy to ignite the mist in brief gold, moss glowing jewel-bright on every stone.

A lily-pond at the wood's quiet edge, its surface unbroken mirror-glass reflecting willow boughs and pale sky, white water-lilies floating as though placed by careful hands, banks smothered in meadow cranesbill and ragged robin.
A wildflower meadow drifting to a line of ancient oaks, poppies and cornflowers standing in drifts like coloured smoke, the tree canopy beyond dark and deep, framing the blossom in shadow and gold.
A woodland lake shimmering faintly luminous under a canopy of oak and ash, its still water holding a perfect inverted world of leaves and sky, a single willow leaning to kiss its own reflection.

A waterfall pool in a sunlit canopy gap, the cascade barely a whisper, the basin clear to every pale pebble, banks mounded with wood sorrel and wild strawberry, ancient oaks pressing close on all sides.

A forest clearing ringed by arching oaks draped with old man's beard, the floor a sea of wood anemone and violet, a spring welling quietly at the centre, its water spreading mirror-still across the moss.
